cards.a: A VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) is a per-tenant virtual routing table plus forwarding instance on a PE router. Each VRF has its own RIB, FIB (CEF), interfaces, and routes, isolating customers even though they share the same physical router and core.

A VRF contains its own RIB (routes), CEF/FIB (forwarding), CE-facing interfaces, routing protocol (eBGP/OSPF/EIGRP/static), and labels (VPN service label). Isolation is at both the control and data plane.

cards.q: How does a VRF differ from the global routing table?
cards.a: The global table is the main table visible to all routes and used for the core/Internet, while a VRF is a per-VRF table seeing only its own routes, shared per customer, and used for L3VPN. The core/global table stays clean of customer prefixes.

cards.q: What is the difference between an RD and an RT?
cards.a: An RD (route distinguisher) makes prefixes unique in MP-BGP, giving identity, while an RT (route target) is the import/export membership policy that controls who shares the VRF.

cards.q: What is the purpose of each VRF configuration command: ip vrf, rd, route-target, ip vrf forwarding?
cards.a: ip vrf NAME creates the VRF; rd sets the route distinguisher; route-target sets import/export policy; and ip vrf forwarding binds an interface to the VRF. BGP uses 'address-family ipv4 vrf' per VRF.

cards.q: How do you configure a VRF to support BGP?
cards.a: Create the VRF with 'ip vrf CUST1', set rd and route-target, bind CE-facing interfaces with 'ip vrf forwarding', and under BGP use 'address-family ipv4 vrf CUST1'.

cards.q: What VRF-aware features need special handling?
cards.a: Static routes, eBGP/iBGP, and OSPF can be per-VRF, and ping/traceroute, SNMP, and Telnet are VRF-aware and often need the 'vrf' keyword, such as 'ping vrf CUST1'.

cards.q: What commands verify VRF routing and forwarding?
cards.a: show ip vrf, show ip vrf detail, show ip route vrf CUST1, show ip cef vrf CUST1, and ping vrf CUST1.

cards.q: What is the likely cause and check when an interface is not in a VRF?
cards.a: The binding is missing, so check show ip vrf and re-apply 'ip vrf forwarding'.

cards.q: What happens to the IP address when you apply 'ip vrf forwarding' to an interface?
cards.a: 'ip vrf forwarding' removes the IP address, so you must re-apply the 'ip address' command afterward.

cards.q: In VRF terms, what do RD and RT each define?
cards.a: RD defines uniqueness (identity) while RT defines membership (who shares the VRF).

cards.q: How does the VRF map to the quick review table?
cards.a: A VRF is a virtual table that isolates the RIB, FIB, and interfaces, uses RD for uniqueness and RT for membership, is bound via 'ip vrf forwarding', uses a BGP AF per VRF, is pinged with 'ping vrf', and serves L3VPN.
